title: End-to-end precision sweep benchmark: latency, p95, tokens/sec vs quality
creator: Maya Chen
description: Build an end-to-end benchmarking harness that runs precision profile sweeps (FP16, INT8, INT4, and mixed modes) across representative workloads and load shapes. The harness must report throughput (tokens/sec), latency distributions (p50/p90/p95/p99), and quality deltas (embedding cosine, ROUGE, token-level divergence, hallucination heuristics) and feed automatic regression detection alerts into Sentry/Slack and a metrics dashboard.
goals: Enable automated, nightly precision sweeps across model variants and dataset prompts
Detect performance regressions (p95 increase) and quality regressions (embedding cosine drop / rouge drop) before rollouts
Provide actionable trade-off matrix for PMs and runtime engineers mapping unit-cost savings to expected quality impact
acceptance_criteria: Harness can run a full sweep (FP16, INT8, INT4, mixed) end-to-end in CI or dedicated runner
Detect p95 latency regressions with alerting within 30 minutes of job completion; false positive rate < 3% on historical baseline
Report tokens/sec and p95 per model/profile per workload and export CSV/JSON and dashboardable Prometheus metrics
Quality checks include embedding cosine similarity, ROUGE-L, and a hallucination proxy. Alerts fire if quality delta exceeds configured thresholds
Documentation (Confluence) and a GitHub PR with test coverage and example config included
test_plan: Synthetic load: constant token rate with OpenAI-style chat sequences, 5k-50k requests over varied seq lengths
Realistic mix: replay sampled production traces from last 30 days (anonymized), stratified by seq length and user type
Scale test: run parallel clients up to the target throughput for Dedicated capacity (simulate 5k concurrent connections at burst)
Quality evaluation: run reference prompts (200 prompt set) and compute embedding cosine, ROUGE, token edit distance, and hallucination heuristics
Regression detector: bootstrap control charts (EWMA) and a nonparametric Mann-Whitney test for quality deltas across runs
metrics_collected: latency_ms: p50, p90, p95, p99, tail by model and profile
KV cache hit rate for prefix-caching experiments
GPU utilization and memory pressure per profile
implementation_notes: Use existing loadgen framework (rust-based runner) with a new quantization profile plugin hook
Leverage 'profile manifests' that map to compilation flags + kernel selection overrides
Store artifacts in s3 with a standard naming schema: s3://redwood-bench/precision-sweeps/{date}/{model}/{profile}/results.json
Regression detection pipeline will run in a scheduled k8s job and write alerts to Slack channel #perf-regressions and create a minimal Sentry issue with run metadata
Keep per-run seeds reproducible; store random seeds and model checkpoints in artifact metadata
architectural_tradeoffs: Eager full-sweep in CI vs. scheduled nightly runs: full CI sweep increases feedback speed but consumes heavy resources; choose nightly for full-sweep and CI quick-checks for smoke

Statistical rigor vs. alert noise: using stricter thresholds reduces false positives but risks missing subtle regressions; we'll combine effect-size thresholds with p-values and require sustained drift over 2 runs
FP16 vs INT8/INT4 quality measurement: INT4 introduces more variance and occasional catastrophic flips—hence include per-sample failure logs to triage edge cases
risks: Noisy production trace replays may increase false positive quality alerts; need better stratification and sampling
INT4 runs may destabilize runtime kernels leading to OOM or hangs—add isolation and crash recovery
Cost: nightly full-sweep across models can increase cloud spend significantly if not throttled
